images.caption: Kailasanatha temple is a megalith carved out of one single basalt rock. Its construction is attributed to king Krishna I (c. 8th century). It is one of the most remarkable cave temples in India because of its size, architecture and sculptural treatment. Ellora Caves, Aurangabad, Maharashtra, India. 600–1000 CE.

images.filename: Bibi Ka Maqbara in the morning hours, Aurangabad, Maharashtra, India 37.jpg
images.caption: The Bibi Ka Maqbara is a tomb located in the city of Aurangabad now known as Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra, India. It was commissioned in 1660 by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb's son, Prince Azam Shah, in the memory of his mother Dilras Banu Begum (posthumously known as Rabia-ul-Durrani). The monuments bears a striking resemblance to the Taj Mahal, the mausoleum of Aurangzeb's mother, Mumtaz Mahal.
